ON THE 4 th OF SEPTEMBER, 2025  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 30097 of 2025  CHAITANYA SHINGANE  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:
 Shri Manish Datt - Senior Advocate with Shri Eshan Datt
Shri Vivek Choudhary - Advocate for the applicant through V.C  Shri C.M. Tiwari - Government Advocate for the responde  Shri Ankit Saxena, learned counsel for the objector.

ORDER This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending his arrest in relation to Crime No.102/2025 registered at Police Station - Awadhpuri, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 409 & 420, 34 of IPC.

2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the present applicant is that he alongwith co-accused persons committed fraud upon the complainant and obtained Rs.3,05,03,601/- from him on the pretext of securing allotment of commercial land belonging to Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. and other government related properties in Bhopal.
Therefore, case was registered against the present applicant and co-accused persons under the aforesaid sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.

It is submitted that FIR was lodged against only NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:42788 2 MCRC-30097-2025 co-accused Kishore Shingane and Jyoti Shingane.
In the FIR, it is not alleged that present applicant has cheated the complainant.

It is further submitted co-accused persons Kishore Shingane and Jyoti Shingane have been granted anticipatory bail by Trial Court on 30.04.2025 and co-accused Dr.Vedant Shingane has been granted regular bail on 28.06.2025.
It is further submitted that an agreement was executed between complainant and co-accused Kishore Shingane on 12.06.2023.
Thereafter, partnership deed was executed on 14.12.2023 between them.
There is no document relating to payment of Rs.55 lacs by the complainant.
The rest of the amount of Rs.2,50,00,000/- has been given in cash.

According to Chaitanya Shingane vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135645048/
1 provision of Income Tax, more than Rs.1,99,000/- cannot be paid in cash.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that there has been settlement between both the parties and vide Ikrarnama executed on 23.08.2024 complainant has accepted that he has received money and in this regard, affidavit has also been filed by complainant.
It is further submitted that father of applicant Kishore Shingane is suffering from diabetes and lost his left leg after surgery.
When the complainant used to come at the residence of applicant, father of applicant told the applicant to look into the matter.
It is further submitted that in both the agreement, there is no allegation on behalf of complainant that signature on both the documents are not of complainant.

Those documents have also been verified by Shri Avdhesh Chandra Namdev filed with I.A. No.20248/2025, who is Retired Government Document Examiner Handwriting Expert and Consultant, who has given report that signatures on both the documents are of complainant.

It is further submitted that applicant has not received any money nor he has executed any document and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42788 3 MCRC-30097-2025 did not participate in the transaction occurred between complainant and father of applicant.
It is further submitted that when earlier three bail applications of co- accused were considered by the Court, at that time, the document dated 09.01.2025 was not filed.
There is no need of custodial interrogation of applicant.
The conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
In these circumstances, applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the objector as well as State have opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant and have submitted that the FIR is not an encyclopedia.

In the FIR,
role of present applicant is also mentioned.
It is further submitted that in this case, offence under Section 467 & 468 of IPC has also been made out.
It is further submitted that father of applicant has obtained signatures of complainant on blank paper, thereafter that blank paper was typed.
In this regard, he has drawn the attention of Court to Ikrarnama (Annexure A/8).
The said document has been filed by present applicant for granting bail.

It is also submitted that mother and father of present applicant, who are co-accused in this case have been granted anticipatory bail by the Trial Court and complainant has filed an application for cancellation of anticipatory bail of his mother and father, which is also pending before this Court.
Therefore, the applicant does not deserve grant of anticipatory bail.
5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the anticipatory bail application filed by the applicant is allowed.

It is directed that if the applicant is arrested by the police then he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer/Arresting Authority.

6. Applicant shall abide by the following conditions under Section 480 (2) NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42788 4 MCRC-30097-2025 of Cr.P.C:-
(a) Applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer as and when required;
Chaitanya Shingane vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135645048/
2

sentences.text: (b) He shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to complainant or witnesses;

(c) He shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court;
(d) He shall not commit similar offence, of which, he is accused or suspected.

(e) He will further abide by the condition enumerated in sub-section (3) of Section 480 of the Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
